description:
FILED s426 (Opus, found while porting StringInterpolation onto InterpScan,
task #388 consumer 3).  PRE-EXISTING: the deleted `parse_braced_expression`
built its mini-document from the RAW block text exactly as the port does.

REPRO (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):

    our $a = "AV";
    print "P:${ \"a\" }\n";      # perl: P:AV
    print "Q:@{[ \"lit\" ]}\n";  # perl: Q:lit   (PCL: Q:lit â this one works)

    PCL on the P line: the emitted CL does not READ â
      "illegal terminating character after a colon: #\""
    and SBCL aborts the load, so the whole program is lost (not one
    statement: the file).

CAUSE: a dq string's block text still carries its backslashes when the
interpolation parser lifts it out, so `\"a\"` has to become `"a"` before
PPI sees it.  `@{ EXPR }` does that (`$expr_str = $self->unescape_string
($expr_str)`); `${ EXPR }` never has.  The asymmetry is now documented in
docs/interp-scan.md (consumer 3, "Residue").

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX â the discriminating measurement, taken:
a blanket `unescape_string` on the `${ }` guts BREAKS the common
`"${\ (2*3) }"` idiom, whose backslash is the REFERENCE operator, not an
escape (`\ ` would be eaten).  perl does not unescape either: it tokenizes
the block in CODE context, where `\"` is a ref-to-a-string and `\"a\"` is
never seen as such because the surrounding quote already ended.  So the
fix is to unescape only the escapes the SURROUNDING quote owns (the
delimiter and `\\`), not the whole string-escape set â and to do it for
BOTH braced-expression arms, from one helper (rule 11).

ACCEPTANCE: the two rows above plus `"${\ (2*3) }"` (must stay 6),
`"@{[ 2*3 ]}"` (6), `"${\ join(q{,}, 1, 2)}"`, and a qq{} / qq() /
heredoc spelling of each â the delimiter differs per quote, so the
"escapes the quote owns" set does too.  Corpus-diff will show the reach.
title: "${ \"a\" }" â the ${ EXPR } interpolation path does not unescape the block text (the @{ EXPR } path does), and PCL then emits UNREADABLE CL: the whole file is lost to an SBCL read error
